cards.explanation: The answer is False. Jesus says, “This sickness will not end in death. No, it is for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it.” He says it plainly as soon as He hears (John 11:4). Keep that sentence in your back pocket, friends, because this story has a few twists coming.

The answer is the glory of God and His Son. Jesus says, “…it is for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it.” He names God and the Son of God right there (John 11:4). It's the reason He gives, friends, and I'll stick to what He actually said.

The answer is that He stays where He is for two days. John says that on hearing Lazarus was sick, Jesus “…stayed where He was for two days…” (John 11:6). It's a surprising thing to read right after the story says He loved this family (John 11:5). John doesn't hand us a reason for the wait, so I won't invent one, friends. I'll just say I think it makes you lean in and keep reading.

The answer is True. The disciples say, “the Jews just tried to stone You, and You are going back there?” (John 11:8). That's the text's own word for it, and it tells you how recent the danger was. They aren't being rude, friends, I think they're worried. When they speak up, it comes out as a question.

The answer is stumble. Jesus says, “If anyone walks in the daytime, he will not stumble, because he sees by the light of this world.” Then He turns it around: whoever walks at night will stumble, because he has no light (John 11:9–10). Walking by daylight means you can see where your feet are going, friends.

The answer is that He's going there to wake him up. Jesus says, “Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I am going there to wake him up” (John 11:11). Notice He calls Lazarus “our friend,” and He's the one doing the going. The disciples have a hard time following what He means by it, friends, as the next verses show.

The answer is True. The disciples reply, “Lord, if he is sleeping, he will get better” (John 11:12). It's perfectly sensible if sleep means sleep. They just don't know yet what Jesus really means, friends, and John explains it in the next verse.

The answer is the death of Lazarus. John says the disciples “…thought that Jesus was talking about actual sleep, but He was speaking about the death of Lazarus” (John 11:13). John steps in to clear it up for us, friends. Jesus will say it in plain words in the very next verse.

The answer is so the disciples may believe. Jesus says, “…for your sake I am glad I was not there, so that you may believe” (John 11:15). He's speaking straight to the disciples, and He says “…for your sake…” That's the reason He gives, friends, so that's the one I'll hold onto.
The answer is False. Jesus finishes His words with, “But let us go to him” (John 11:15). Lazarus is dead, and He still says to go. That little “But” is carrying a lot of weight, friends.

The answer is that Thomas says, “Let us also go, so that we may die with Him.” Thomas, the disciple also called Didymus, says it to his fellow disciples (John 11:16). He knows the danger in Judea, since they'd just reminded Jesus about the stoning (John 11:8). I think those are the words of a man who isn't backing out, friends. He's ready to go with Jesus, and that's a lot of courage.
